To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of citrate tablets to serums to be stored for a period of 7 days at 25° will preserve the activity of the prostatic acid phosphatic fraction of the serum acid phosphatases.
the addition of citrate to serums containing the prostatic fraction (PF) of acid phosphatase is effective in stabilizing and preserving the original activity for at least 2 weeks at 4° and 25°.

the addition of citrate tablets to buffer serums at pH 6.2 was the only effective method for the preservation, at 25°, of the prostatic acid phosphotase activity of serums for a period of at least 7 days.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable, reproducible and simple method for the preservation and transport of serum prostatic fraction of acid phosphatase.
the development of a method to preserve the prostatic fraction activity of acid phosphatase in serums shipped to a central laboratory.
the development of a simple method for the preservation and stabilization of the prostatic phosphatase activity in serums.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of 1.5 gm. of citrate tablets (pH 6.2) per 100 cc. of serum, followed by refrigeration, is the most satisfactory method for preserving the activity of serum prostatic phosphatase.

the addition of citrate tablets to serums at the time of collection and shipment, to buffer the serumes at pH 6, will preserve the activity of the prostatic acid phosphatas fraction for 1 week at room temperature.
citrate, as a buffer, is an effective stabilizer for the preservation of the prostatic acid phosphatase activity in serums stored at room temperature for at least 1 week.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a citrate buffer at pH 6,2 and a temperature of 25° C. will preserve the prostatic acid phosphatic activity for at least 5 to 6 days.
the prostatic fraction activity of serum is stable for at least 3 days at room temperature and for at least 1 week at 4°.
the prostatic fraction is stable at pH 6-7 and at temperatures up to at least 30°C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now preserve serum prostatic acid phosphate activity for at least 1 week at room temperature.
we can use the same methods and tools to analyze and compare the stability and preservation of different types of acid phosphatases.
we have shown that the addition of a pH 6.0 buffer to serum can preserve the activity for at least 3 weeks at room temperature.
